findings.summary: Percent-encoded slashes decoded before routing, enabling path-prefix authorisation bypass
findings.description:
## Affected

`github.com/malcolmston/express` **<= 0.4.0** (all published versions). No fix released.

Parity case: `basic-encoded-path` (`parity/express/cases/routing-basic.json`).
Oracle: express 4.21.2.

## Upstream vs port

`newRequest` takes the routing path from the already-decoded `r.URL.Path`
(`request.go:40`):

```go
path: cleanPath(r.URL.Path),
```

Go's `net/http` decodes `%2F` to `/` in `URL.Path`, so a `%2F` that the client sent *inside* a
single path segment becomes a segment separator before any route is matched.

| request | express 4.21.2 | this port |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GET /a%2Fb` against route `/a/b` | 404 (no match; `req.url` keeps `%2F`) | **200** (matches) |

Upstream matches on the raw (still-encoded) path via `path-to-regexp` and applies
`decodeURIComponent` per captured parameter after the match.

## Impact (attacker terms)

Percent-encoding a slash is the standard way to keep an untrusted value confined to one path
segment. Decoding before routing means a value that was escaped specifically so it *could
not* traverse into another route now does exactly that. This is an authorisation-bypass and
path-confusion primitive rather than a cosmetic routing difference:

* a prefix-mounted guard such as `app.Use("/admin", requireAdmin)` can be sidestepped by a
  request whose encoded form does not carry the guarded prefix but whose decoded form routes
  into a handler behind it;
* `/files/:name` receiving `name=a%2F..%2Fb` yields a parameter that traverses segments,
  feeding path traversal into any handler that treats `:name` as a single opaque token;
* any front-door proxy, WAF or reverse-proxy ACL that decides on the raw request target will
  disagree with the port's routing decision for the same request.

Exploitability depends on the application using path-prefix middleware or segment-scoped
parameters, which is common but not universal - hence a primitive rather than a guaranteed
bypass.

## Reproduction

```go
app := express.New()
app.Get("/a/b", func(req *express.Request, res *express.Response, next express.Next) { res.Send("HIT") })
// GET /a%2Fb  ->  200 "HIT"   (express 4.21.2: 404)
```

## Suggested fix

Match against `r.URL.EscapedPath()` (falling back to the path component of `RequestURI`) and
decode each captured parameter individually after the match, matching `path-to-regexp` +
`decodeURIComponent` upstream.

## Severity rationale

Graded **medium** (CVSS-style "moderate"): it reliably breaks a security-relevant invariant (segment escaping) and
yields authorisation-bypass and traversal primitives, but realising impact requires the
consuming application to rely on path-prefix guards or segment-scoped parameters. Lower than
the default-404 XSS in the same module, which needs no cooperating application code.

findings.summary: Reflected XSS in the default 404 handler (request path echoed into unescaped text/html)
findings.description: ## Affected `github.com/malcolmston/express` **<= 0.4.0** (all published versions). No fix released. Parity cases: `default404-miss`, `default404-miss-method` (`parity/express/cases/errors.json`, harness in `Malcolmston/go`). Oracle: express 4.21.2. ## Upstream vs port `Application.ServeHTTP` terminates an unmatched request with: ```go res.Status(http.StatusNotFound).Send("Cannot " + req.Method() + " " + req.Path()) ``` `Response.Send` defaults a `string` body to `Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8` (`response.go:145-148`), and `req.Path()` is `r.URL.Path`, i.e. **percent-decoded**. The request target is therefore reflected, unescaped, into an HTML document. Upstream express delegates to `finalhandler`, which HTML-escapes the path *and* sends `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none'` and `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`. The port sends neither header. ## Impact (attacker terms) Reflected XSS reachable on **every** application built on this module that does not install its own terminal 404 handler - which is the default, out-of-the-box configuration. The attacker needs only to get a victim to open a crafted URL on the target origin; there is no prerequisite application code, no authentication, and no unusual configuration. Script then runs in the application's origin with access to its cookies, tokens and same-origin API surface. The two response headers upstream sends exist precisely to make this class of bug unexploitable, and both are absent, so there is no defence-in-depth fallback. ## Reproduction ```go app := express.New() app.Get("/ok", func(req *express.Request, res *express.Response, next express.Next) { res.Send("ok") }) ``` ``` GET /%3Cimg%20src=x%20onerror=alert(1)%3E -> 404, Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8 body: Cannot GET / ``` Upstream express 4.21.2 returns the same path HTML-escaped, under `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none'` and `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`. ## Suggested fix HTML-escape the reflected method and path (or send `text/plain`), and set `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` and `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none'` on both the default 404 path and `finalError`. ## Severity rationale Graded **high**: script execution in the application origin in the default configuration, requiring only a crafted URL, with both upstream mitigating headers missing. Not graded critical because the impact is client-side (no server-side code execution or data access) and requires victim interaction with an attacker-supplied URL.
